harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (RHEL 7.9) so new user passwords must be at least 12 characters and use at least 3 character classes, enforced via pam_pwquality. Discovered and corrected a subtlety: pwquality's default per-class length credits (dcredit/ucredit/lcredit/ocredit=1) reduce the effective minlen floor when extra classes are present, so minlen=12 alone did not guarantee a hard 12-char minimum. Set minlen=12, minclass=3, and zeroed all four credit values in /etc/security/pwquality.conf so both constraints apply independently. Verified enforcement live via passwd for real test users, then performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted node1 with `shutdown -r now`, confirmed boot_id changed after the node came back, and re-verified the policy config and PAM enforcement survived and still work correctly post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (RHEL 7.9), confirmed libpwquality/pam_pwquality already installed and wired into /etc/pam.d/system-auth and password-auth
Captured baseline: empty pwquality.conf overrides, backed up original config
Appended minlen=12 and minclass=3; discovered via pwscore/passwd testing that credit system silently reduced the effective minimum length
Added dcredit=0, ucredit=0, lcredit=0, ocredit=0 to make minlen a hard floor independent of character classes
Verified via pwscore and real passwd changes for a temporary test user that length<12, classes<3, and combined violations are correctly rejected, and a compliant 12-char/3-class password is accepted
Cleaned up test user pwtestuser
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime, active config, PAM stack)
Restarted node1 via `shutdown -r now` (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until reachable again; confirmed boot_id changed, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified config persisted and PAM enforcement still functions correctly post-restart using a second temporary test user, then cleaned it up

evidence.requirement: Baseline: pwquality already available in PAM stack, no active length/class overrides
evidence.summary: Confirms libpwquality installed, pam_pwquality.so referenced in system-auth/password-auth, and pwquality.conf had no active overrides before the change
Shows initial config write of minlen=12 and minclass=3 (later refined)

evidence.requirement: Diagnosed and fixed credit-reduction issue so 12-char minimum is a hard floor
evidence.summary: Root-caused why an 8-char/3-class password only required length 9 (credit system reducing minlen by class count), then added dcredit/ucredit/lcredit/ocredit=0 and re-verified boundary cases: 11-char/4-class fails on length, 12-char/2-class fails on class count, 12-char/3-class passes

evidence.requirement: End-to-end enforcement via real PAM password change (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: Real passwd changes for pwtestuser show 11-char/4-class and 12-char/2-class rejected, 12-char/3-class accepted; test user removed afterward

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart baseline for mandatory restart protocol
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 95e2f83d..., boot time, active pwquality.conf content, and PAM stack lines before reboot
shutdown -r now issued in background; command returned 'reboot issued' before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node unreachable during restart, then changed boot identity proving restart occurred
evidence.summary: Two consecutive connection timeouts while node1 was rebooting, followed by successful reconnect showing new boot_id 0b6c6870..., differing from the pre-restart 95e2f83d...
who -b shows new boot time 2026-09-29 10:37; pwquality.conf still contains minlen=12, minclass=3, and all four credits=0; PAM stack still references pam_pwquality.so

evidence.requirement: Post-restart functional re-verification of policy enforcement
evidence.summary: Fresh test user pwtestuser2: 11-char/4-class password change rejected for being shorter than 12, 12-char/3-class password change accepted; test user removed afterward
